title: request-fidelity-cost-and-provenance-playbook-2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook defines how the runtime produces per-request provenance and cost-attribution records and how teams should use those signals to investigate fidelity regressions, quantify unit economics, and support billing/chargeback for Dedicated/private deployments. It bridges kernel scheduling telemetry, KV cache instrumentation, model variant metadata, token accounting, and accelerator utilization.

Scope

- Applies to all requests processed by the inference serving runtime (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Covers the attribution pipeline from request start to final token emission (including fallbacks and partial responses).
- Excludes offline training/compilation jobs and batch-only offline analytics (those have separate costing).

Goals

1. Produce a stable, compact per-request attribution record in <= 20ms after response completion.
2. Attribute cost to the most granular levers available: model-variant, kernel-hours, GPU-time-ms, energy-estimate, and cache-hit-paths.
3. Ensure provenance contains reproducible routing and fallback decisions for debugging quality regressions.
4. Support downstream consumers: billing, Optimize recommendations, SRE incident correlation, and product analytics.

Definitions

- Request provenance: immutable trace of routing decisions, model variants, kernel hints, and cache interactions for a single request.
- Cost delta: estimated incremental cost caused by a request, expressed in micro-dollars and normalized per-token.
- Fidelity tag: classification (high/medium/low) of whether the served result used lower-fidelity fallbacks (quantized model, distilled variant, partial decode).

Observability signals to collect

Collect these signals at the request boundary and include them in the attribution record:

- request_id, tenant_id, route_id, model_id, model_version
- sequence_length_requested, sequence_length_generated, prompt_token_count, completion_token_count
- scheduling_slot_id, kernel_id, kernel_version, kernel_wall_time_ms, kernel_cpu_ms
- gpu_active_ms, gpu_sm_percent, gpu_power_watts_estimate
- kvcache_hits, kvcache_prefetches, kvcache_miss_reason
- queue_wait_ms, preemption_events, priority_class, admission_decision_reason
- fallback_sequence (ordered list of fallbacks applied), fallback_reasons
- feature_flags_active (list), quantization_profile, batch_size_at_execution
- streaming_chunks_count (if streamed) and partial_response_flags

Data model (compact payload)

We publish a compact JSON for downstream consumers. Example payload (every field is optional but prefer consistent presence):

{\
  \"request_id\": \"r_01E9YX5J\",\
  \"tenant_id\": \"t-acme\",\
  \"model_id\": \"redwood-7b-q4\",\
  \"model_version\": \"2026-01-10\",\
  \"prompt_tokens\": 42,\
  \"completion_tokens\": 128,\
  \"kernel_profile\": [{\"kernel_id\": \"matmul_v2\", \"wall_ms\": 32, \"cpu_ms\": 1}],\
  \"gpu_ms\": 45,\
  \"kvcache_hits\": 12,\
  \"kvcache_misses\": 3,\
  \"fallbacks\": [\"quantized-fallback\"],\
  \"fidelity_tag\": \"medium\",\
  \"estimated_cost_micros\": 1250\
}

Attribution algorithm (high-level)

1. Token baseline: compute token-cost baseline using model catalog per-token weights (prompt vs completion).
2. Kernel augmentation: add kernel wall-time * kernel-specific energy and price coefficient (kernel hinting table maintained by runtime-perf team).
3. Accelerator overheads: map gpu_ms and power_estimate to a per-tenant proportional cost using timestamped capacity allocation (handles shared Dedicated pools).
4. Cache crediting: subtract estimated saved cost from kvcache_hits using prefix-length-weighted credit.
5. Fallback penalty: add a small adder for fidelity loss (used by product analytics), tagged separately from monetary estimates.

Implementation notes and tables

- Kernel hint table (canonical source: /infra/config/kernel-hints): maps kernel_id -> {energy_coeff, base_latency_ms, price_coeff}. Teams must version updates and include migration notes.

- Example cost coefficients (illustrative):
| source                 | coefficient example | unit               | comment                  |
|------------------------|---------------------|--------------------|--------------------------|
| model_token_prompt     | 0.00035             | micro$ per token   | prompt tokens cheaper    |
| model_token_completion | 0.00080             | micro$ per token   | completion tokens more   |
| kernel_price_coeff     | 0.12                | micro$ per ms      | multiply by wall_ms      |
| gpu_power_coeff        | 0.00003             | micro$ per watt-ms | used for energy estimates|

Runbook: Investigate a high-cost or fidelity-regression request

1. Find request: query the attribution index by request_id or tenant/time window. Example Kibana query:
- request_id:r_01E9YX5J OR (tenant_id:t-acme AND @timestamp:[now-1h TO now])

2. Inspect top-level fields: model_id, kernel_profile, gpu_ms, kvcache_hits. If estimated_cost_micros >> baseline estimate, continue.

3. Check scheduling and admission logs: verify queue_wait_ms and preemption_events. If queue_wait_ms > 50ms, escalate to SRE (page on-call).

4. Validate model variant: confirm model_version and quantization_profile. If fidelity_tag==low or fallback sequence contains \"distilled\" or \"quantized-fallback\", open a fidelity regression ticket and attach the attribution payload.

5. Reproduce in sandbox: use the request-replay tool with preserved RNG and decision overrides to force the same kernel and cache paths. Command example:

# replay tool (developer sandbox)
redwood-replay --request r_01E9YX5J --preserve-routing --force-cache-prefetch

6. If kernel wall times dominate, run the microbenchmark for the identified kernel on matching hardware (ref: benchmarking/kernel-microbench-runbook).

7. If kvcache misses are unexpectedly high, follow kvcache warmup checklist: verify shard placement, prefetch hints, and session-affinity.

Policies and thresholds

- Attribution latency: target <= 20ms 95th. If backlog > 1000 records/min over target, open a capacity incident. Owner: telemetry-team.
- Fidelity alerts: emit an automatic alert when fallback rate for a model-version exceeds 2% for 30m rolling window. Owner: runtime-ml-product.
- Cost drift: trigger a cost-anomaly signal when tenant-level per-token cost deviates > 20% vs previous 72h. Owner: billing-ops.

Data retention and privacy

- Attribution records are retained 90 days in hot storage, 2 years in compressed cold storage.
- Records may contain prompt_token counts but not prompt text in hosted mode; private deployments may opt-in to richer payloads.
- Sensitive tenant identifiers should be hashed for analytics exports. See /security-and-compliance/data-management for procedures.

Rollout checklist for the attribution pipeline

1. Unit tests for kernel hinting translation and cost math.
2. Integration test: ingest 1k synthetic requests across concurrency shapes and validate sum(est_costs) ~= measured billing samples within 5%.
3. Canary: enable attribution at 1% of traffic with sidecar publish to test index; monitor attribution-latency and mismatch-rate.
4. Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours with manual signoffs.

Consumer integration patterns

- Billing: consume estimated_cost_micros on a per-tenant aggregation schedule (hourly). Keep a reconciliation process between estimated_cost_micros and actual metered GPU-hours (weekly).
- Optimize: use per-request kernel footprints to suggest quantization profiles and batching knobs for the tenant.
- SRE: correlate attribution records with trace IDs and kernel traces for incident correlation.

Operational ownership and contacts

- Runtime telemetry pipeline: telemetry-team (oncall: telemetry@redwood.ai)
- Kernel hint table owner: perf-kernel-team (lead: Jonah Kim)
- Billing & reconciliation: finance-ops (lead: Priya Menon)

- Should estimated_cost_micros incorporate full electricity regionalization or remain approximate? (owner: finance-ops)
